page: Microsoft Azure D8ds_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture and hosted on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor operating at 4.2 GHz, configured with 8 dedicated vCPUs spanning 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The processor features 480 MB of shared L3 cache and supports vector and matrix acceleration instructions, including AVX-512 and Intel AMX. System memory is sized at 32.0 GB, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM allocation. Local ephemeral storage consists of a 472 GB NVMe SSD, while discrete GPU acceleration is not present.

Benchmark measurements position the D8ds_v7 primarily in the middle tier for compute and memory operations, with notable strengths in specific single-threaded tasks. Multi-core performance registered a stress-ng score of 9,302.94, while PassMark CPU achieved 16,691.48. Memory throughput delivers 89.09 GB/sec for uncached large block reads and 39.04 GB/sec for writes. The instance performs in the top quartile for data compression workloads, attaining 35.05 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip compression and 15.08 GB/sec in single-threaded bzip3 decompression. In lightweight machine learning scenarios without dedicated GPUs, it achieves 270.06 tokens per second in text generation for a small 135M parameter model. Networked and database benchmarks recorded static web serving throughput of 16.54 GB/sec and 15.0 million Redis SET operations per second.

From a cost and architectural efficiency standpoint, the inclusion of 472 GB of local NVMe SSD storage reduces reliance on external persistent block volumes for temporary files, swap space, and local caching. Integrated AMX and AVX-512 instructions allow modest vector and integer calculations directly on the CPU without incurring the cost overhead of dedicated GPU resources. However, workloads requiring heavy concurrent parallelism or large in-memory databases may encounter bottlenecks from the 4-core physical limit and 32 GB RAM ceiling. The configuration is appropriate for web serving, microservices, continuous integration runners, lightweight caching nodes, and ETL data transformation pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure D8ds_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine equipped with 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor clocked at 4.2 GHz. Supported by 32 GB of system memory, the instance maintains a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio alongside a 472 GB local NVMe SSD for fast ephemeral storage. It features instruction-level hardware acceleration including Intel AMX and AVX-512, without discrete GPU hardware. Benchmark evaluations show solid mid-tier multi-threaded compute, supported by high single-core compression rates of 35.05 GB/sec in gzip and 270.06 tokens per second for small-model LLM text generation. Redis caching performance registers at 15.0 million SET operations per second. The embedded local SSD offers storage cost efficiency for intermediate data handling. D8ds_v7 is well suited for web hosting, CI/CD workloads, data transformation pipelines, and distributed cache tiers.
